claims.text: A thin Nb interlayer between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating will suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion with an Nb interlayer will maintain coating integrity.
The Nb interlayer will maintain oxidation resistance under both subcritical-water and high-temperature steam exposures.
A conventional elemental Cr coating on zirconium alloy exhibits premature failure because of Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
The proposed intervention is a thin, continuous Nb barrier deposited directly between the Zr-alloy surface and the Cr coating.
The intended routine-service condition is high-pressure subcritical water at approximately 360°C.
The intended accident condition is steam at approximately 1000°C for a short duration.
The Nb interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier limiting atomic migration between Cr and the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Nb has low mutual solubility with Cr.
Nb has low mutual solubility with Zr.
Low mutual solubility at the interfaces retards Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Retarded Cr–Zr interdiffusion preserves the metallic coating microstructure at high temperature.
Preservation of the coating microstructure sustains its oxidation-protective properties at high temperature.
Relative to a direct Cr coating, the Nb-interlayered coating will exhibit reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to a direct Cr coating, the Nb-interlayered coating will exhibit less spallation or premature failure.
Relative to a direct Cr coating, the Nb-interlayered coating will provide improved oxidation protection in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
Long-term irradiation effects and possible chemical interactions under neutron flux are unresolved.
